# tryck

> Typed errors for TypeScript. Functions return `Result` values instead of throwing; `yield*` inside `gen` unwraps them like Rust's `?`. Only the error classes you name are caught: every other throw stays a defect.

Fourteen functions, no methods, no runtime. Import everything from `tryck`.

## The rules

- Results are plain data: `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, error }`. Check `result.ok`, or compare in tests with `expect(r).toEqual(ok(1))`.
- Sync in, sync out. `function*` gives a `Result`; `async function*` gives a `Promise` of one. In an async body write `yield* await promise`.
- Catch by class: `attempt(fn, SyntaxError)`. Translate a foreign error into your own with a pair: `attempt(fn, [SyntaxError, InvalidJson])`.
- Name errors with `class NotFound extends taggedError('NotFound')<{ id: string }> {}`. The fields `_tag`, `name`, `stack` and `toJSON` are reserved.
- Fold a result with `match(result, { ok, NotFound, err })`. Every `_tag` needs a handler unless `err` is present.
- Guard inside `gen` with `return yield* err(e)`, not `yield* err(e)`.
- There is no `.map`, `.andThen` or `isOk`. Compose with `gen`, translate with `mapErr`, handle with `recover` or `match`.

## Functions

- `ok(value)`, `err(error)`: build a result
- `attempt(fn, ...catches)`: run `fn`, turning the listed classes into an `Err`
- `safe(fn, ...catches)`: wrap a function once with `attempt`
- `when(Class, test)`: catch a class only when `test` passes
- `parse(schema, input)`: validate with any Standard Schema (Zod, Valibot, ArkType) into `Result<T, ValidationError>`
- `revive(sent, { NotFound })`: rebuild a result that came from JSON, errors included
- `gen(function* () {})`: chain results with `yield*`
- `all(results)`: collect several results into one
- `mapErr(result, fn)`: translate an error
- `recover(result, handlers)`: handle errors by `_tag` and drop them from the type
- `match(result, handlers)`: turn a result into a value
- `unwrap(result)`: get the value or throw the error
- `taggedError(tag)`: define an error class with a literal `_tag`
